title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 4. Beholding the Ghats, Wells and Other Places of Mathura-mandala
html:
Krishnadasa shows the Lord Mathura: its walls and gates, Kamsa's palace, the prison and "the place where He passed water" as the infant Krishna, the houses of Uddhava, the washerman, the garland-maker, Kubja, Vasudeva and Ugrasena, the arena, the Deity of Gatashrama, the twelve ghats, the Well of Kamsa and other holy places; having gone round the city, the Lord takes His meal in Krishnadasa's house

Verse 1

शृणुष्व करुणासिन्धो माथुरस्य कथां शुभाम्।
आदौ मधुपुरीं पश्य राजधानीं सुशोभनाम्॥१॥

śṛṇuṣva karuṇāsindho māthurasya kathāṁ śubhām|
ādau madhupurīṁ paśya rājadhānīṁ suśobhanām||1||

shrinushva — hear; karuna-sindho — O ocean of compassion; mathurasya — of the land of Mathura; katham — the account; shubham — auspicious; adau — first; madhupurim — Madhupuri; pashya — behold; rajadhanim — the royal capital; sushobhanam — most beautiful.

1"Hear, O ocean of compassion, the auspicious account of the land of Mathura. Behold first Madhupuri, the most beautiful royal capital.

Verse 2

त्रिषु परिसरेषूच्चैर्दुर्गं प्राचीरमुत्तमम्।
पुर्याः पूर्वे दक्षिणाभिमुखे वहति भानुजा॥२॥

triṣu parisareṣūccairdurgaṁ prācīramuttamam|
puryāḥ pūrve dakṣiṇābhimukhe vahati bhānujā||2||

trishu — on three; parisareshu — sides; uchchaih — lofty; durgam — a fortress; prachiram — a rampart; uttamam — excellent; puryah — of the city; purve — on the east; dakshina-abhimukhe — southward; vahati — flows; bhanu-ja — the daughter of the Sun.

2On three sides a lofty fortress wall surrounds it, an excellent rampart, and to the east of the city the daughter of the Sun1 flows southward.

Verse 3

उत्तरे दक्षिणे च द्वौ द्वारौ रत्नकवाटिकौ।
राजवाटीं नैरृते स्यान्नानारत्नविभूषिताम्॥३॥

uttare dakṣiṇe ca dvau dvārau ratnakavāṭikau|
rājavāṭīṁ nairṛte syānnānāratnavibhūṣitām||3||

uttare — in the north; dakshine — in the south; cha — and; dvau — two; dvarau — gates; ratna-kavatikau — with jewelled doors; raja-vatim — the royal palace; nairrite — in the south-west; syat — there is; nana-ratna-vibhushitam — adorned with many jewels.

3To the north and to the south are two gates with jewelled doors; in the south-west is the royal palace, adorned with many jewels,

Verse 4

पूर्वोत्तराभ्यां द्वारैश्च रत्नवज्रैः समन्विताम्।
वाट्या उत्तरपार्श्वे च वेदीं राजोपवेशनाम्॥४॥

pūrvottarābhyāṁ dvāraiśca ratnavajraiḥ samanvitām|
vāṭyā uttarapārśve ca vedīṁ rājopaveśanām||4||

purva-uttarabhyam — on the east and north; dvaraih — with gates; cha — and; ratna-vajraih — with jewels and diamonds; samanvitam — furnished; vatyah — of the palace; uttara-parshve — on the north side; cha — and; vedim — the dais; raja-upaveshanam — where the king sits.

4with gates on the east and north set with jewels and diamonds; and on the north side of the palace is the dais where the king sat.

Verse 5

वायव्यां खलु पुर्याश्च बन्धनागारमेव च।
तस्यापि दक्षिणे मूत्रस्थानं पश्य यथासुखम्॥५॥

vāyavyāṁ khalu puryāśca bandhanāgārameva ca|
tasyāpi dakṣiṇe mūtrasthānaṁ paśya yathāsukham||5||

vayavyam — in the north-west; khalu — indeed; puryah — of the city; cha — and; bandhana-agaram — the prison; eva — indeed; cha — and; tasya — of it; api — further; dakshine — to the south; mutra-sthanam — "the place where (Krishna) passed water"; pashya — behold; yatha-sukham — at leisure.

5In the north-west of the city is the prison, and to the south of it behold at Your leisure 'the place where He passed water.'

Verse 6

अस्य विवरणं वक्ष्ये शृणु सावहितं प्रभो।
कंसाद्भीतो हि भगवान् वसुदेव उदारधीः॥६॥

asya vivaraṇaṁ vakṣye śṛṇu sāvahitaṁ prabho|
kaṁsādbhīto hi bhagavān vasudeva udāradhīḥ||6||

asya — of this; vivaranam — the explanation; vakshye — I shall tell; shrinu — listen; sa-avahitam — attentively; prabho — O Lord; kamsat — of Kamsa; bhitah — afraid; hi — for; bhagavan — the venerable; vasudevah — Vasudeva; udara-dhih — noble-minded.

6I shall tell You how it came about — listen attentively, O Lord. The noble Vasudeva, in fear of Kamsa,

Verse 7

कृष्णमादाय नन्दस्य गोष्ठं गच्छन्महामनाः।
ज्ञात्वा क्रोडस्थितं कृष्णं मूत्रयन् सत्वरं मुदा॥७॥

kṛṣṇamādāya nandasya goṣṭhaṁ gacchanmahāmanāḥ|
jñātvā kroḍasthitaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ mūtrayan satvaraṁ mudā||7||

krishnam — Krishna; adaya — taking; nandasya — of Nanda; goshtham — to the cowherd settlement; gacchan — going; maha-manah — great-hearted; jnatva — realising; kroda-sthitam — held on his lap; krishnam — Krishna; mutrayan — passing water; satvaram — quickly; muda — gladly.

7took Krishna and, great-hearted, was carrying Him to the cowherd settlement of Nanda. Realising that Krishna on his lap was passing water, he quickly and gladly

Verse 8

अयं प्रस्तरमारुह्य स्थितः स च क्षणं प्रभो।
कृष्णस्य मूत्रचिह्नोऽयं वर्तते प्रस्तरोपरि॥८॥

ayaṁ prastaramāruhya sthitaḥ sa ca kṣaṇaṁ prabho|
kṛṣṇasya mūtracihno'yaṁ vartate prastaropari||8||

ayam — this; prastaram — onto the stone; aruhya — climbing; sthitah — stood; sah — he; cha — and; kshanam — for a moment; prabho — O Lord; krishnasya — of Krishna; mutra-chihnah — mark of urine; ayam — this; vartate — remains; prastara-upari — on the stone.

8climbed onto this stone and stood on it for a moment, O Lord; and this mark of Krishna's water remains upon the stone to this day.

Verse 9

अतएव जनाः सर्वे मूत्रस्थानं वदन्ति हि।
उद्धवस्य गृहं पश्य दक्षिणेऽस्य तदेव तम्॥९॥

ataeva janāḥ sarve mūtrasthānaṁ vadanti hi|
uddhavasya gṛhaṁ paśya dakṣiṇe'sya tadeva tam||9||

atah eva — therefore; janah — the people; sarve — all; mutra-sthanam — "the place where He passed water"; vadanti — call it; hi — indeed; uddhavasya — of Uddhava; griham — the house; pashya — behold; dakshine — to the south; asya — of it; tat eva tam — there it is.

9That is why all the people call this 'the place where He passed water.' And to the south of it — behold — is the house of Uddhava."

Verse 10

श्रुत्वा हुङ्कारं कुर्वन्तं प्रभुं दृष्ट्वा द्विजोत्तमः।
भीतः किल सुमेधाश्च कृताञ्जलिरुवाच ह॥१०॥

śrutvā huṅkāraṁ kurvantaṁ prabhuṁ dṛṣṭvā dvijottamaḥ|
bhītaḥ kila sumedhāśca kṛtāñjaliruvāca ha||10||

shrutva — hearing; hunkaram — a roar; kurvantam — making; prabhum — the Lord; drishtva — seeing; dvija-uttamah — the best of brahmanas; bhitah — alarmed; kila — indeed; su-medhah — wise; cha — and; krita-anjalih — with joined palms; uvacha — said; ha — indeed.

10Hearing this, the Lord gave a thunderous roar. Seeing Him roar, the best of brahmanas was alarmed, and, wise as he was, he joined his palms and said:

Verse 11

शृणुष्व वचनं कृष्ण लीलाकारिन् जगद्गुरो।
स्थिरः सन् दर्शनादेव सुखमेव भवेद्ध्रुवम्॥११॥

śṛṇuṣva vacanaṁ kṛṣṇa līlākārin jagadguro|
sthiraḥ san darśanādeva sukhameva bhaveddhruvam||11||

shrinushva — hear; vachanam — my word; krishna — O Krishna; lila-karin — O performer of pastimes; jagat-guro — O Teacher of the world; sthirah — calm; san — being; darshanat — from seeing; eva — alone; sukham — joy; eva — surely; bhavet — will be; dhruvam — certainly.

11"Hear my word, O Krishna, performer of pastimes, O Teacher of the world: be calm — the mere sight of these places will surely bring You joy.

Verse 12

रजकस्य गृहं पश्योद्धवस्य गृहपूर्वतः।
रजकस्य गृहात्पूर्वे मालाकारगृहं तथा॥१२॥

rajakasya gṛhaṁ paśyoddhavasya gṛhapūrvataḥ|
rajakasya gṛhātpūrve mālākāragṛhaṁ tathā||12||

rajakasya — of the washerman; griham — the house; pashya — behold; uddhavasya — of Uddhava; griha-purvatah — east of the house; rajakasya — of the washerman; grihat — from the house; purve — to the east; mala-kara-griham — the house of the garland-maker; tatha — likewise.

12Behold: east of Uddhava's house is the house of the washerman2, and east of the washerman's house is the house of the garland-maker.

Verse 13

अस्यापि दक्षिणे कुब्जागृहं देवविनिर्मितम्।
कुब्जाया नैरृते रङ्गस्थलं परमशोभनम्॥१३॥

asyāpi dakṣiṇe kubjāgṛhaṁ devavinirmitam|
kubjāyā nairṛte raṅgasthalaṁ paramaśobhanam||13||

asya — of it; api — further; dakshine — to the south; kubja-griham — Kubja's house; deva-vinirmitam — built by the gods; kubjayah — from Kubja's; nairrite — to the south-west; ranga-sthalam — the arena; parama-shobhanam — most splendid.

13South of it is the house of Kubja3, built by the gods, and south-west of Kubja's house is the splendid arena.

Verse 14

रङ्गस्थलस्याग्निकोणे वसुदेवगृहं शुभम्।
उग्रसेनगृहं चास्य चैशान्यां विधिना कृतम्॥१४॥

raṅgasthalasyāgnikoṇe vasudevagṛhaṁ śubham|
ugrasenagṛhaṁ cāsya caiśānyāṁ vidhinā kṛtam||14||

ranga-sthalasya — of the arena; agni-kone — in the south-east corner; vasudeva-griham — Vasudeva's house; shubham — auspicious; ugrasena-griham — Ugrasena's house; cha — and; asya — of it; cha — and; aishanyam — in the north-east; vidhina — by the Creator; kritam — built.

14In the south-east corner of the arena is the auspicious house of Vasudeva, and to the north-east of it is the house of Ugrasena4, built by the Creator.

Verse 15

अस्यापि दक्षिणे पश्य कृष्णमूर्तिं गतश्रमाम्।
दृष्ट्वा तां श्रीगौरचन्द्रः पुलकाङ्गो बभूव ह॥१५॥

asyāpi dakṣiṇe paśya kṛṣṇamūrtiṁ gataśramām|
dṛṣṭvā tāṁ śrīgauracandraḥ pulakāṅgo babhūva ha||15||

asya — of it; api — further; dakshine — to the south; pashya — behold; krishna-murtim — the Deity of Krishna; gata-shramam — Gatashrama ("Freed from Weariness"); drishtva — seeing; tam — it; shri-gaura-chandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; pulaka-angah — His body thrilling; babhuva — became; ha — indeed.

15And south of it behold the Deity of Krishna as Gatashrama5." Seeing it, Sri Gaurachandra thrilled all over.

Verse 16

विश्रामं श्रमशान्तं च कंसखालीति संज्ञकम्।
प्रयागं तिन्दुनामानं सप्तर्षिमोक्षकोटिकम्॥१६॥

viśrāmaṁ śramaśāntaṁ ca kaṁsakhālīti saṁjñakam|
prayāgaṁ tindunāmānaṁ saptarṣimokṣakoṭikam||16||

vishramam — Vishrama; shrama-shantam — Shramashanta; cha — and; kamsa-khali — Kamsakhali; iti — thus; samjnakam — called; prayagam — Prayaga; tindu-namanam — the one named Tindu; saptarshi-moksha-kotikam — Saptarshi, Moksha and Koti.

16"Vishrama, Shramashanta, the ghat called Kamsakhali, Prayaga, the one named Tindu, Saptarshi, Moksha, Koti,

Verse 17

बोधिशिवगणेशादिद्वादशघट्टसंज्ञकम्।
क्रमाद्दक्षिणतो ज्ञेयं तीर्थराजं महाप्रभम्॥१७॥

bodhiśivagaṇeśādidvādaśaghaṭṭasaṁjñakam|
kramāddakṣiṇato jñeyaṁ tīrtharājaṁ mahāprabham||17||

bodhi-shiva-ganesha-adi-dvadasha-ghatta-samjnakam — Bodhi, Shiva, Ganesha and the rest, called the twelve ghats; kramat — in order; dakshinatah — southward; jneyam — to be known; tirtha-rajam — a king of holy places; maha-prabham — of great splendour.

17Bodhi, Shiva, Ganesha and the rest — these are called the twelve ghats6; know that they follow one another southward — a king among holy places, full of great splendour.

Verse 18

पुर्याश्च दक्षिणे रङ्गभूमिं कृष्णसुखप्रदाम्।
अस्याश्च दक्षिणे कूपं पश्य श्रीकृष्णहेतवे॥१८॥

puryāśca dakṣiṇe raṅgabhūmiṁ kṛṣṇasukhapradām|
asyāśca dakṣiṇe kūpaṁ paśya śrīkṛṣṇahetave||18||

puryah — of the city; cha — and; dakshine — in the south; ranga-bhumim — the arena; krishna-sukha-pradam — giving joy to Krishna; asyah — of it; cha — and; dakshine — to the south; kupam — the well; pashya — behold; shri-krishna-hetave — on account of (against) Sri Krishna.

18In the south of the city is the arena that gave joy to Krishna7, and to the south of it behold the well dug against Sri Krishna:

Verse 19

कंसेन खनितं तेन कंसकूपमितीर्यते।
अस्यापि नैरृते कुण्डमगस्त्येन विनिर्मितम्॥१९॥

kaṁsena khanitaṁ tena kaṁsakūpamitīryate|
asyāpi nairṛte kuṇḍamagastyena vinirmitam||19||

kamsena — by Kamsa; khanitam — dug; tena — therefore; kamsa-kupam — the Well of Kamsa; iti — thus; iryate — it is called; asya — of it; api — further; nairrite — to the south-west; kundam — a pond; agastyena — by Agastya; vinirmitam — made.

19Kamsa dug it, and so it is called the Well of Kamsa. And to the south-west of it is a pond made by Agastya8.

Verse 20

पुर्याश्चोत्तरतः सप्तसामुद्रकुण्डसंज्ञकम्।
प्रस्तरं पश्य देवक्याः पुत्रनाशाय निर्मितम्॥२०॥

puryāścottarataḥ saptasāmudrakuṇḍasaṁjñakam|
prastaraṁ paśya devakyāḥ putranāśāya nirmitam||20||

puryah — of the city; cha — and; uttaratah — to the north; sapta-samudra-kunda-samjnakam — (the pond) called Sapta-samudra ("Seven Oceans"); prastaram — the stone; pashya — behold; devakyah — of Devaki; putra-nashaya — for destroying the sons; nirmitam — prepared.

20To the north of the city is the pond called Sapta-samudra ('Seven Oceans'). Behold the stone prepared for destroying the sons of Devaki9

Verse 21

कंसेनेति हसन्तं तं पुनः प्राह हसन् द्विजः।
अस्याप्युत्तरतः पश्य लिङ्गं भूतेश्वरं प्रभो॥२१॥

kaṁseneti hasantaṁ taṁ punaḥ prāha hasan dvijaḥ|
asyāpyuttarataḥ paśya liṅgaṁ bhūteśvaraṁ prabho||21||

kamsena — by Kamsa; iti — thus; hasantam — laughing; tam — to Him; punah — again; praha — said; hasan — laughing; dvijah — the brahmana; asya — of it; api — further; uttaratah — to the north; pashya — behold; lingam — the linga; bhuteshvaram — Bhuteshvara; prabho — O Lord.

21by Kamsa." And, laughing, the brahmana spoke again to the laughing Lord: "To the north of it, O Lord, behold the linga Bhuteshvara10.

Verse 22

पुनश्च यमुनां पश्य सरस्वतीसमन्विताम्।
दशाश्वमेधघट्टं च तत्रैव सोमतीर्थकम्॥२२॥

punaśca yamunāṁ paśya sarasvatīsamanvitām|
daśāśvamedhaghaṭṭaṁ ca tatraiva somatīrthakam||22||

punah — again; cha — and; yamunam — the Yamuna; pashya — behold; sarasvati-samanvitam — joined by the Sarasvati; dashashvamedha-ghattam — the Dashashvamedha Ghat; cha — and; tatra eva — right there; soma-tirthakam — the Soma-tirtha.

22And behold too the Yamuna joined by the Sarasvati, and the Dashashvamedha Ghat, and right there the Soma-tirtha,

Verse 23

कण्ठाभरणसंज्ञं च नागतीर्थाभिधानकम्।
संयमाख्यककुण्डादि पुरीप्रसरसङ्कुलम्॥२३॥

kaṇṭhābharaṇasaṁjñaṁ ca nāgatīrthābhidhānakam|
saṁyamākhyakakuṇḍādi purīprasarasaṅkulam||23||

kanthabharana-samjnam — the one called Kanthabharana; cha — and; naga-tirtha-abhidhanakam — the one named Naga-tirtha; samyama-akhyaka-kunda-adi — the pond named Samyama and others; puri-prasara-sankulam — crowding the whole extent of the city.

23the tirtha called Kanthabharana, the one named Naga-tirtha, the pond named Samyama and the other holy places that crowd the whole extent of the city."

Verse 24

एवं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्वा मथुरां परमेश्वरः।
भिक्षां चकार भिक्षान्नं कृष्णदासगृहे सुखम्॥२४॥

evaṁ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā mathurāṁ parameśvaraḥ|
bhikṣāṁ cakāra bhikṣānnaṁ kṛṣṇadāsagṛhe sukham||24||

evam — thus; pradakshini-kritva — circumambulating; mathuram — Mathura; parama-ishvarah — the Supreme Lord; bhiksham chakara — took alms; bhiksha-annam — the food of alms; krishnadasa-grihe — in the house of Krishnadasa; sukham — happily.

24Thus the Supreme Lord went round Mathura, keeping it on His right, and happily took His alms — His meal — in the house of Krishnadasa.

Verse 25

स्मृत्वाथ कृष्णदासेन सेवितं चरणद्वयम्।
श्रीकृष्णपरमानन्दमाधुर्यं कथयन् प्रभुः॥२५॥

smṛtvātha kṛṣṇadāsena sevitaṁ caraṇadvayam|
śrīkṛṣṇaparamānandamādhuryaṁ kathayan prabhuḥ||25||

smritva — remembering; atha — then; krishnadasena — by Krishnadasa; sevitam — served; charana-dvayam — His two feet; shri-krishna-parama-ananda-madhuryam — the sweetness of the supreme bliss of Sri Krishna; kathayan — telling; prabhuh — the Lord.

25Then, while Krishnadasa served His two feet, the Lord, remembering, spoke of the sweetness of the supreme bliss of Sri Krishna.

Thus ends the fourth sarga, "Beholding the Ghats, Wells and Other Places of Mathura-mandala" (Mathura-mandala-ghatta-kupadi-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The daughter of the Sun: the Yamuna.
  2. The washerman: Kamsa's royal dyer, whom Krishna slew on entering Mathura; the garland-maker is Sudama, who crowned Krishna and Balarama with garlands (Bhagavata Purana 10.41).
  3. Kubja: the hunchbacked maidservant of Kamsa whom Krishna made straight (Bhagavata Purana 10.42).
  4. Ugrasena: Kamsa's father, deposed by him and restored to the throne by Krishna.
  5. Gatashrama ("Freed from Weariness"): the Deity of Krishna resting after His victory over Kamsa, at the Vishrama Ghat.
  6. Ghats: bathing steps on the bank of the Yamuna.
  7. The arena (ranga-bhumi) where Krishna and Balarama overcame Kamsa's wrestlers.
  8. Agastya: the great sage, a hero of the Puranas.
  9. Devaki: Krishna's mother; Kamsa killed her infants by dashing them against a stone.
  10. Bhuteshvara ("Lord of Beings"): a linga of Shiva, the guardian of Mathura.
